sentences.text: HRH1 appears tolerant of loss-of-function variation in humans, with a gnomAD LOEUF of 1.15 and an Open Targets constraint factor of 0.431.
Mouse knockouts show 21 phenotypes, led by immune system and homeostasis/metabolism phenotypes (6 each), with an Open Targets mouse KO score of -0.690.
61 approved drugs act on HRH1, but the antagonist astemizole was withdrawn in 1998 in many countries, including the United States, for cardiotoxicity and immune system toxicity.

Curated safety events link HRH1 inhibition to cardiac arrhythmia and decreased allergic responses, and link activation to bronchoconstriction, decreased blood pressure, abdominal cramps and allergic responses of flare, flush and wheal.

Because many HRH1 antagonists remain approved, astemizole's cardiotoxicity may partly reflect compound-specific off-target activity rather than HRH1 blockade alone, although the curated cardiac arrhythmia event for HRH1 inhibition means an on-target contribution cannot be excluded.
Doxepin carries a US Black Box Warning for psychiatric toxicity, and its top FAERS signals include suicide attempt (reports 105, LLR 205.2) and somnolence (reports 93, LLR 111.1).
Somnolence with HRH1 antagonists may reflect on-target blockade of central H1 receptors, consistent with brain expression (z-score 0.80) and behavior/neurological knockout phenotypes.
Methapyrilene was withdrawn in 1979 for carcinogenicity, whereas HRH1 itself is not listed as a cancer driver gene.
Post-marketing evidence is thin for most listed antagonists, since astemizole, carbinoxamine, dibenzepin and methapyrilene show no top FAERS signals.
Only 6 of the 61 approved drugs are listed, so the safety profiles of the remaining HRH1 drugs are not covered by this pack.

Clozapine's hematological, cardiotoxicity and infectious disease black box warnings, with neutropenia as a top FAERS signal, may arise from off-target or compound-specific effects rather than DRD2 itself, since this pack gives no DRD2-specific hematological evidence.

sentences.text: ADRB2 is a G alpha (s)-coupled adrenoceptor in Signal Transduction pathways, and 40 approved drugs act on this target.

Curated safety events for ADRB2 concentrate in the cardiovascular system, including bradycardia, cardiac contractility, decreased blood pressure and heart failure, alongside bronchospasm and decreased blood potassium.

Several ADRB2 drugs have been withdrawn, including fenoterol for respiratory toxicity, metaproterenol for cardiotoxicity and dilevalol for hepatotoxicity, while albuterol and levosalbutamol carry Black Box Warnings.
FAERS signals for agonists are dominated by asthma, wheezing and dyspnoea, whereas the antagonist esmolol shows cardiac arrest and circulatory collapse signals.

The cardiac and potassium findings plausibly reflect on-target beta-adrenergic signalling in heart and blood, so both agonism and antagonism could carry cardiovascular liability depending on direction of modulation.

The airway FAERS signals for agonists may partly reflect the treated asthma population or loss of effect rather than direct drug toxicity, consistent with the 'therapeutic product effect incomplete' signal.
Expression is broad, with a distribution factor of -1.000 and highest z-scores in skin 2.23 and lung 1.58, limiting tissue selectivity.
Genetic constraint is weak (LOEUF 0.91), yet mouse knockouts show 25 phenotypes with a KO score of -0.776, spanning vision, skeleton and immune classes.
The Black Box Warnings for albuterol and levosalbutamol do not state a class or year, so the specific nature of those warnings cannot be assessed from this pack.
Dilevalol has no FAERS signals listed, so its hepatotoxicity withdrawal cannot be corroborated by post-marketing data here.

The shared cardiotoxicity and abuse-potential signals may be on-target, reflecting increased synaptic noradrenaline after SLC6A2 inhibition in cardiovascular and central nervous system tissues.

Desipramine signals such as ileus, urinary retention and QRS complex prolongation may partly reflect off-target activity of tricyclics rather than SLC6A2 itself, consistent with the ToxCast receptor binding event.

sentences.text: ADRB1 is a well-precedented target, with 27 approved drugs acting on it, and the listed agents are small-molecule antagonists or inhibitors that map to G alpha (s) signalling and adrenoceptor pathways.

These bradycardia and hypotension signals likely reflect on-target blockade of beta-1-mediated cardiac G alpha (s) signalling, consistent with high GTEx expression in heart (z-score 1.96).

Several withdrawals were for non-cardiac toxicities, including practolol (dermatological toxicity, immune system toxicity, occular toxicity, ototoxicity, 1975) and metipranolol (occular toxicity, 1990).
Because these withdrawal classes are not reflected in the curated on-target safety events, they may arise from compound-specific off-target properties rather than ADRB1 modulation itself.
Expression is also elevated in lung (z-score 2.52), and bronchospasm is a curated safety event, which warrants monitoring of respiratory effects.
